identity.title: Single breath count (count aloud on one full inspiration; <20 signals weak respiratory muscles)

technique.how: Patient sits upright, takes a maximal inspiration, then counts aloud from 1 upward in a normal voice at about two numbers per second (2 Hz; use a metronome/app if available) without taking another breath. Record the highest number reached; take the best of 3 attempts. Repeat serially (e.g. every 4-6 h) in evolving neuromuscular weakness.
technique.prerequisites: Patient can speak and follow commands; note dysarthria or facial weakness that slows counting.
technique.contraindications: Unreliable in severe dysarthria/aphasia, uncooperative or delirious patients, and after recent airway/oral surgery.

interpretation.positive_finding: A low count signals reduced vital capacity: SBC <=5 predicted need for mechanical ventilation in GBS with sensitivity 0.91 and specificity 0.95; SBC <=21 identified VC <20 mL/kg in hospitalized patients (sens 0.94, spec 0.77); SBC <25 detected MG exacerbation with sensitivity 0.80.
interpretation.negative_finding: A count >=20-25 makes severe respiratory muscle weakness (VC <20 mL/kg) unlikely; in GBS a count >19 had 95% sensitivity for ruling out need for ventilation, and in ALS a count above the cut-off had 100% sensitivity for FVC <50% predicted.
interpretation.pitfalls: Counting speed and voice loudness change the number (unpaced counts run higher); bulbar weakness, pain, COPD and anxiety lower counts without diaphragm weakness; thresholds differ by disease and study (5-41), so trend serial counts rather than fixing on one number.
interpretation.changes_what: Count <20 (or falling >20% in 24 h): obtain FVC/NIF and ABG, escalate monitoring, prepare for airway support; count comfortably >25 and stable: continue serial checks.

estimates.target_condition: Need for intubation/mechanical ventilation in GBS (SBC <=5)
estimates.population: 94 GBS patients (age 6-70) with serial SBC at 2 Hz, India, neurology inpatients
estimates.reference_standard: Intubation per modified ABG criteria (PaO2 <60 with PaCO2 >50, or pH <7.3)
estimates.quote: At SBC 5, need for MV could be predicted with a sensitivity of 90.6% and specificity of 95.2%

estimates.target_condition: Need for mechanical ventilation in GBS (SBC >19 rules out)
estimates.population: GBS patients (Kalita 2020 cohort as tabulated by systematic review)
estimates.quote: SBCT>19 had sensitivity of 95% in ruling out the need for mechanical ventilation

estimates.population: MG patients (cohort as tabulated in systematic review; attribution ambiguous between refs 17 and 21)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical MG exacerbation (as defined in primary study; not viewable)
estimates.quote: SBCT < 25 had sensitivity of 80% in diagnosing myasthenia exacerbation

estimates.population: Hospitalized patients with a variety of diseases (Bartfield 1994 cohort as tabulated in systematic review)
estimates.quote: SBCT of 21 or less had a sensitivity and specificity of 94.4% and 76.62% for VC <20 ml/kg

estimates.target_condition: Vital capacity <80% predicted (count <41) in neuromuscular dystrophy
estimates.population: Patients with neuromuscular dystrophy (single study within meta-analysis)
estimates.quote: a count lower than 41 for a VC below 80% of predicted in patients with neuromuscular dystrophy (Sensitivity = 89% and Specificity = 62%)
SBCpp had 100% sensitivity and 60% specificity (area under curve (AUC) = 0.696) for predicting FVCpred <50%

sources.citation: Bhandari SK, Bist A, Ghimire A. Single breath count test and its applications in clinical practice: a systematic review. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2024;86(4):2113-2118.
Kalita J, Kumar M, Misra UK. Serial single breath count is a reliable tool for monitoring respiratory functions in Guillain-Barre Syndrome. J Clin Neurosci. 2020;72:50-56.

Elsheikh B, Arnold WD, Gharibshahi S, Reynolds J, Freimer M, Kissel JT. Correlation of single-breath count test and neck flexor muscle strength with spirometry in myasthenia gravis. Muscle Nerve. 2016;53(1):134-136.
Delmondes GMB, Couto NFS, Correia Junior MGA, et al. Single breath counting technique to assess pulmonary function: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Breath Res. 2023;18(1).
Quinn C, McMillan CT, Owegi MA, et al. Single breath counting is an effective screening tool for forced vital capacity in ALS. Amyotroph Lateral Scler Frontotemporal Degener. 2021;22(7-8):528-534.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not substitute SBC for spirometry/NIF when a decision to intubate is imminent, or in patients with bulbar dysarthria, aphasia or delirium where counting is unreliable.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: SBC <=10, a fall >20% over 24 h, inability to complete a sentence, paradoxical breathing or rising PaCO2 indicate impending respiratory failure - ICU and airway readiness now.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Paced (2 Hz) counting has good intra- and inter-examiner reproducibility (Delmondes 2023 review); unpaced counts vary with speaking speed and voice, so use the same method serially.

extraction_notes: Primary GBS estimate is verbatim from the abstract of Kalita 2020 (PMID 31982274); LRs computed by extractor. Three estimates are taken from Table 3 of the open-access 2024 systematic review (PMID 38576972, PMC10990392) because the primary papers (Bartfield 1994 Ann Emerg Med; the MG-exacerbation study) are not accessible: the review's Table 3 attributes the MG '<25, sensitivity 80%' row to Kannan Kanikannan 2014 (a GBS paper) while its text cites ref 21 (Kukulka 2020, telephonic SBCT in MG) - attribution is inconsistent, flagged for the verifier. The neuromuscular-dystrophy and mixed-hospitalized numbers are corroborated by the abstract of Delmondes 2023 meta-analysis (PMID 37875103: count 21 for VC 20 mL/kg sens 94% spec 77%). The '<20' threshold in the title is a common clinical convention; the literature cut-offs range 5-41 depending on outcome. Elsheikh 2016 (PMID 26437790) shows correlation with FVC only (no cut-off accuracy in abstract; PMC copy contains header only), cited for MG context. No CIs were available for any estimate.
